ShapeEngine

Class Polygon

Namespace
ShapeEngine.Geometry.PolygonDef
Assembly
ShapeEngine.dll

Represents a 2D polygon defined by a sequence of points in counter-clockwise order, providing geometric operations, containment and intersection tests, convex hull computation, triangulation, randomization, and shape manipulation utilities.

Remarks

Points should be provided in CCW order for correct geometric calculations. Use FixWindingOrder() or MakeCounterClockwise() if your points are in clockwise (CW) order.

  • A convex polygon is a polygon where all interior angles are less than 180°, and every line segment between any two points inside the polygon lies entirely within the polygon. In other words, no vertices "point inward."
  • A concave polygon is a polygon that has at least one interior angle greater than 180°, and at least one line segment between points inside the polygon passes outside the polygon. This means it has at least one "caved-in" or inward-pointing vertex.

IsClockwise()

Determines if the polygon's winding order is clockwise.

public bool IsClockwise()

Returns

bool

True if clockwise; otherwise, false.

IsConvex()

Determines if the polygon is convex.

public bool IsConvex()

Returns

bool

True if convex; otherwise, false.

Remarks

  • A convex polygon is a polygon where all interior angles are less than 180°, and every line segment between any two points inside the polygon lies entirely within the polygon. In other words, no vertices "point inward."
  • A concave polygon is a polygon that has at least one interior angle greater than 180°, and at least one line segment between points inside the polygon passes outside the polygon. This means it has at least one "caved-in" or inward-pointing vertex.

IsConvex(List<Vector2>)

Determines if a polygon defined by a list of vertices is convex.

public static bool IsConvex(List<Vector2> vertices)

Parameters

vertices List<Vector2>

The list of vertices representing the polygon.

Returns

bool

True if the polygon is convex; otherwise, false.

Remarks

  • Convex: A convex polygon is a polygon where all interior angles are less than 180°, and every line segment between any two points inside the polygon lies entirely within the polygon. This means none of its vertices "point inward," and the polygon does not have any indentations.
  • Concave: A concave polygon has at least one interior angle greater than 180° and at least one vertex that points inward (self-intersecting).
